text.p: Mexican financial group BBV-Probursa said on Thursday its net profit in the first half of 1997 was 209 million pesos, up from 149 million pesos in the year ago period.
The company's director general, Antonio Galdiz, said at a news conference that its banking unit earned 177 million pesos in the first six months of the year, compared with 35 million pesos in 1996.
He said the company's banking unit closed June with a capitalization index of 13.47 percent, compared with the year-ago level of 12.6 percent in 1996.
In the second quarter, the group's net profits were 120 million pesos, 35 percent above the first quarter of the year, Galdiz added.

Share capital for the banking unit at the end of June was 3.188 billion, an increase of 60 percent compared with the year-ago period. Loan loss provisions were at 75.4 percent at the end of June, up from 72.7 percent the previous year, BBV-Probursa said.
